column3: NASB moves “on behalf of men” after “appointed.”
“Exercise forbearance” is rendered “deal gently,” and “those going astray” “misguided”; “encompassed” is rendered “beset.”
NASB moves “as for the people, so also for himself” to the end.
NASB supplies “so as.” The quotation is in capitals.
“To the age” is rendered “forever,” and NASB adds “passage.”
“Concerning this” is rendered “Concerning him”; “difficult in interpretation to speak” is rendered “hard to explain,” and “sluggish in the hearings” “dull of hearing.”
“The principles of the beginning” is rendered “the elementary principles.”
“Through constant use” is rendered “because of practice,” and “distinguish” “discern.”
